WHAT IS THE ISSUE:
- Root cause: A newly fitted wire spool is defective or its brake tension is too tight, creating excess resistance that drops feed speed below the minimum and triggers the WM‑101 wire feed motor overload alarm. (Evidence: alarm pattern tied to new spool + graph cause “Defective or Poor‑Quality Wire Spool” and “Wire Spool Braking Too Tight”)
- What is different: This occurrence is the first documented overload directly linked to a new spool installation; prior overloads were associated with feed‑rate drops or drive‑roll wear. (Evidence: Alarm Agent “What is different this time”)

WHAT IS THE IMPACT:
- Production impact: Line stopped; estimated downtime ≈ 1 hour for inspection, spool replacement and burn‑in. (Knowledge Graph estimate)
- Safety risk: HIGH – motor overload can cause motor burnout and wire‑feed damage; LOTO required before any maintenance.
- Financial impact: Approximate loss of one hour of production plus potential scrap of parts welded during the fault event.

HOW CRITICAL IS IT:
- HIGH
- Justification: Fault requires immediate LOTO and production stop; three‑alarm systemic trigger exists in SOP and the current alarm follows a new spool defect, meeting the HIGH minimum criteria.

HOW TO ADDRESS IT:
- Immediate action:
  Step 1: Safety — Initiate LOTO: isolate power at main disconnect, apply personal lock and tag with name/date, verify machine cannot be enabled. (Knowledge Graph LOTO requirement)
  Step 2: Diagnosis — Stop welding; release wire tension at drive rolls; manually pull wire through liner and note resistance. Inspect the newly installed spool for kinks, rust, inconsistent diameter, or excessive brake tension. (SOP procedure + graph spool‑brake cause)
  Step 3: Fix — If spool is defective or brake too tight, replace the spool with a known‑good GSW‑WIRE‑xxxx spool; re‑set drive‑roll tension to “finger‑tight plus one quarter turn.” Do NOT keep adjusting tension beyond this setting. (SOP tension spec, mandatory warning)
  Step 4: Verify — Run a test bead; perform the mandatory burn‑in procedure: run wire at 5.0 m/min for 30 seconds, then continue for 10 minutes. Wire feed instability during the first 5 minutes is EXPECTED and not a fault. (WI‑WM101‑001 mandatory burn‑in)
  Step 5: Quality — Quarantine all parts welded during the fault event for inspection before release. (SOP quality inspection flag)

- Root cause fix (permanent solution):
  • Implement a pre‑install inspection checklist for new wire spools to verify spool condition and brake tension before fitting; reject any spool showing defects or excessive brake resistance.

- Preventive action (stops recurrence):
  • Add a SOP amendment requiring visual and tactile verification of spool brake tension and wire integrity after each spool change; record verification in the shift log.
  • Schedule a quarterly audit of spool inventory to ensure only compliant spools are stocked.
  • Train operators on the “Do NOT keep adjusting tension” warning and proper spool‑change procedure.

- Who to notify:
  • Maintenance Supervisor
  • Production Control
  • Quality Assurance (for part quarantine)
  • Shift Lead
